title: Introduce AWS SQS for decoupled communications in atlaspay-ledger
problem: Tight coupling leads to cascading failures across the backend. We need asynchronous messaging to guarantee eventual consistency and fault tolerance.
context: Direct HTTP calls between atlaspay-ledger and other services create hard dependencies. When downstream systems are down, transactions fail immediately, causing poor customer experience.
decision: Integrate AWS SQS to enable asynchronous, event-driven communication between atlaspay-ledger and downstream microservices.
alternatives:
1. Keep synchronous REST APIs but increase timeouts and retry limits.
2. Introduce an HTTP webhook callback system.
3. Deploy AWS SQS as a centralized event broker.
lessons_learned: Requires handling out-of-order execution, ensuring message idempotency in processors, and setting up telemetry for queue lags. Deployed in DEP-0041. Caused incident INC-0022 due to: Cache stampede in atlaspay-ledger for metadata queries. Rolled back or mitigated.

title: Implement Redis cache layer for security-scanner
problem: High load on databases and slow API responses due to repeated queries for the same static configuration and user profile data.
context: security-scanner performs heavy database reads for static or slow-moving configurations, putting unnecessary read load on our primary databases and increasing endpoint latency.
decision: Implement Redis as a distributed caching layer for security-scanner endpoints.
alternatives:
1. Add read replicas to the primary database.
2. Use in-memory application caching.
3. Deploy a centralized Redis caching cluster.
lessons_learned: Cache invalidation logic must be added to all update operations. Cache eviction policies (LRU) must be configured. Deployed in DEP-0066. Caused incident INC-0031 due to: Database connection pool exhaustion on security-scanner. Rolled back or mitigated.

title: Use Kubernetes to deploy platform-monitoring to AWS
problem: Deployment takes over 40 minutes, and we lack auto-scaling. Small configuration drift on VMs makes debugging environments difficult.
context: Our current deployment model using manual VM provisioning is slow, error-prone, and makes scaling applications dynamically very difficult during high load.
decision: Standardize all microservice deployments, starting with platform-monitoring, on Kubernetes hosted on AWS.
alternatives:
1. Script VM creation using custom Ansible and AMI images.
2. Deploy directly to AWS ECS.
3. Implement a complete Kubernetes container orchestration architecture.
metrics_before_after: Average cost went from 50.74 USD/day to 55.95 USD/day (+5.21 / +10.3%).
lessons_learned: All services must be containerized (Dockerfiles written). Helm charts must be created, and CI/CD pipelines updated. Deployed in DEP-0081. Caused incident INC-0039 due to: Message lag spike on Kafka partition for platform-monitoring. Rolled back or mitigated.

title: Adopt MongoDB for fusionerp-payroll database storage
problem: High read/write latency during peak traffic periods resulting in database connection pools exhausting, causing intermittent errors in downstream services.
context: Our current database strategy for fusionerp-payroll is experiencing scalability limitations under peak loads. We need a solution that can handle high throughput, support strong consistency, and scale horizontally.
decision: Migrate the primary storage of fusionerp-payroll to MongoDB to leverage its native scaling and high availability features.
alternatives:
1. Scale vertical resources on existing systems.
2. Implement a distributed cache layer (e.g. Redis) as a buffer.
3. Migrate to a multi-master distributed DB like MongoDB.
lessons_learned: Developers must learn MongoDB-specific query optimization. We must set up migration scripts and operational monitoring for the new clusters. Deployed in DEP-0106. Caused incident INC-0050 due to: Unoptimized query on fusionerp-payroll database after release. Rolled back or mitigated.

title: Introduce RabbitMQ for decoupled communications in fusionerp-payroll

title: Introduce RabbitMQ for decoupled communications in insightcrm-analytics
problem: Tight coupling leads to cascading failures across the backend. We need asynchronous messaging to guarantee eventual consistency and fault tolerance.
context: Direct HTTP calls between insightcrm-analytics and other services create hard dependencies. When downstream systems are down, transactions fail immediately, causing poor customer experience.
decision: Integrate RabbitMQ to enable asynchronous, event-driven communication between insightcrm-analytics and downstream microservices.
alternatives:
1. Keep synchronous REST APIs but increase timeouts and retry limits.
2. Introduce an HTTP webhook callback system.
3. Deploy RabbitMQ as a centralized event broker.
lessons_learned: Requires handling out-of-order execution, ensuring message idempotency in processors, and setting up telemetry for queue lags. Deployed in DEP-0733. Caused incident INC-0352 due to: Message lag spike on Kafka partition for insightcrm-analytics. Rolled back or mitigated.

title: Introduce RabbitMQ for decoupled communications in atlaspay-portal
problem: Tight coupling leads to cascading failures across the backend. We need asynchronous messaging to guarantee eventual consistency and fault tolerance.
context: Direct HTTP calls between atlaspay-portal and other services create hard dependencies. When downstream systems are down, transactions fail immediately, causing poor customer experience.
decision: Integrate RabbitMQ to enable asynchronous, event-driven communication between atlaspay-portal and downstream microservices.
alternatives:
1. Keep synchronous REST APIs but increase timeouts and retry limits.
2. Introduce an HTTP webhook callback system.
3. Deploy RabbitMQ as a centralized event broker.
lessons_learned: Requires handling out-of-order execution, ensuring message idempotency in processors, and setting up telemetry for queue lags. Pending deployment and operations feedback.

title: Introduce RabbitMQ for decoupled communications in cloudsync-storage
problem: Tight coupling leads to cascading failures across the backend. We need asynchronous messaging to guarantee eventual consistency and fault tolerance.
context: Direct HTTP calls between cloudsync-storage and other services create hard dependencies. When downstream systems are down, transactions fail immediately, causing poor customer experience.
decision: Integrate RabbitMQ to enable asynchronous, event-driven communication between cloudsync-storage and downstream microservices.
alternatives:
1. Keep synchronous REST APIs but increase timeouts and retry limits.
2. Introduce an HTTP webhook callback system.
3. Deploy RabbitMQ as a centralized event broker.
lessons_learned: Requires handling out-of-order execution, ensuring message idempotency in processors, and setting up telemetry for queue lags. Pending deployment and operations feedback.

title: Introduce Kafka for decoupled communications in novacommerce-cart
problem: Tight coupling leads to cascading failures across the backend. We need asynchronous messaging to guarantee eventual consistency and fault tolerance.
context: Direct HTTP calls between novacommerce-cart and other services create hard dependencies. When downstream systems are down, transactions fail immediately, causing poor customer experience.
decision: Integrate Kafka to enable asynchronous, event-driven communication between novacommerce-cart and downstream microservices.
alternatives:
1. Keep synchronous REST APIs but increase timeouts and retry limits.
2. Introduce an HTTP webhook callback system.
3. Deploy Kafka as a centralized event broker.
lessons_learned: Requires handling out-of-order execution, ensuring message idempotency in processors, and setting up telemetry for queue lags. Pending deployment and operations feedback.

title: Adopt DynamoDB for insightcrm-analytics database storage

decision: Migrate the primary storage of insightcrm-analytics to DynamoDB to leverage its native scaling and high availability features.

title: Introduce Kafka for decoupled communications in atlaspay-ledger

title: Introduce RabbitMQ for decoupled communications in visionai-inference
problem: Tight coupling leads to cascading failures across the backend. We need asynchronous messaging to guarantee eventual consistency and fault tolerance.
context: Direct HTTP calls between visionai-inference and other services create hard dependencies. When downstream systems are down, transactions fail immediately, causing poor customer experience.
decision: Integrate RabbitMQ to enable asynchronous, event-driven communication between visionai-inference and downstream microservices.
alternatives:
1. Keep synchronous REST APIs but increase timeouts and retry limits.
2. Introduce an HTTP webhook callback system.
3. Deploy RabbitMQ as a centralized event broker.
lessons_learned: Requires handling out-of-order execution, ensuring message idempotency in processors, and setting up telemetry for queue lags. Pending deployment and operations feedback.

context: Direct HTTP calls between fusionerp-core and other services create hard dependencies. When downstream systems are down, transactions fail immediately, causing poor customer experience.
decision: Integrate NATS to enable asynchronous, event-driven communication between fusionerp-core and downstream microservices.
alternatives:
1. Keep synchronous REST APIs but increase timeouts and retry limits.
2. Introduce an HTTP webhook callback system.
3. Deploy NATS as a centralized event broker.
lessons_learned: Requires handling out-of-order execution, ensuring message idempotency in processors, and setting up telemetry for queue lags. Pending deployment and operations feedback.

historical_evolution.event: Decision formulated and accepted as ADR-0389.
Jira ticket FC16-29 created for tracking implementation.

title: Implement Redis cache layer for atlaspay-portal
problem: High load on databases and slow API responses due to repeated queries for the same static configuration and user profile data.
context: atlaspay-portal performs heavy database reads for static or slow-moving configurations, putting unnecessary read load on our primary databases and increasing endpoint latency.
decision: Implement Redis as a distributed caching layer for atlaspay-portal endpoints.
alternatives:
1. Add read replicas to the primary database.
2. Use in-memory application caching.
3. Deploy a centralized Redis caching cluster.
lessons_learned: Cache invalidation logic must be added to all update operations. Cache eviction policies (LRU) must be configured. Pending deployment and operations feedback.

title: Adopt MongoDB for cloudsync-storage database storage

context: Our current database strategy for cloudsync-storage is experiencing scalability limitations under peak loads. We need a solution that can handle high throughput, support strong consistency, and scale horizontally.
decision: Migrate the primary storage of cloudsync-storage to MongoDB to leverage its native scaling and high availability features.
alternatives:
1. Scale vertical resources on existing systems.
2. Implement a distributed cache layer (e.g. Redis) as a buffer.
3. Migrate to a multi-master distributed DB like MongoDB.
lessons_learned: Developers must learn MongoDB-specific query optimization. We must set up migration scripts and operational monitoring for the new clusters. Pending deployment and operations feedback.

title: Use Kubernetes to deploy platform-monitoring to AWS
problem: Deployment takes over 40 minutes, and we lack auto-scaling. Small configuration drift on VMs makes debugging environments difficult.
context: Our current deployment model using manual VM provisioning is slow, error-prone, and makes scaling applications dynamically very difficult during high load.
decision: Standardize all microservice deployments, starting with platform-monitoring, on Kubernetes hosted on AWS.
alternatives:
1. Script VM creation using custom Ansible and AMI images.
2. Deploy directly to AWS ECS.
3. Implement a complete Kubernetes container orchestration architecture.
metrics_before_after: Average cost went from 151.40 USD/day to 153.46 USD/day (+2.06 / +1.4%).
lessons_learned: All services must be containerized (Dockerfiles written). Helm charts must be created, and CI/CD pipelines updated. Pending deployment and operations feedback.

title: Adopt DynamoDB for atlaspay-gateway database storage
problem: High read/write latency during peak traffic periods resulting in database connection pools exhausting, causing intermittent errors in downstream services.
context: Our current database strategy for atlaspay-gateway is experiencing scalability limitations under peak loads. We need a solution that can handle high throughput, support strong consistency, and scale horizontally.
decision: Migrate the primary storage of atlaspay-gateway to DynamoDB to leverage its native scaling and high availability features.
alternatives:
1. Scale vertical resources on existing systems.
2. Implement a distributed cache layer (e.g. Redis) as a buffer.
3. Migrate to a multi-master distributed DB like DynamoDB.
lessons_learned: Developers must learn DynamoDB-specific query optimization. We must set up migration scripts and operational monitoring for the new clusters. Pending deployment and operations feedback.

title: Use Nomad to deploy visionai-training to AWS
problem: Deployment takes over 40 minutes, and we lack auto-scaling. Small configuration drift on VMs makes debugging environments difficult.
context: Our current deployment model using manual VM provisioning is slow, error-prone, and makes scaling applications dynamically very difficult during high load.
decision: Standardize all microservice deployments, starting with visionai-training, on Nomad hosted on AWS.
alternatives:
1. Script VM creation using custom Ansible and AMI images.
2. Deploy directly to AWS ECS.
3. Implement a complete Nomad container orchestration architecture.
metrics_before_after: Average cost went from 170.54 USD/day to 172.36 USD/day (+1.82 / +1.1%).
lessons_learned: All services must be containerized (Dockerfiles written). Helm charts must be created, and CI/CD pipelines updated. Pending deployment and operations feedback.

title: Introduce NATS for decoupled communications in platform-k8s-mesh
problem: Tight coupling leads to cascading failures across the backend. We need asynchronous messaging to guarantee eventual consistency and fault tolerance.
context: Direct HTTP calls between platform-k8s-mesh and other services create hard dependencies. When downstream systems are down, transactions fail immediately, causing poor customer experience.
decision: Integrate NATS to enable asynchronous, event-driven communication between platform-k8s-mesh and downstream microservices.
alternatives:
1. Keep synchronous REST APIs but increase timeouts and retry limits.
2. Introduce an HTTP webhook callback system.
3. Deploy NATS as a centralized event broker.
lessons_learned: Requires handling out-of-order execution, ensuring message idempotency in processors, and setting up telemetry for queue lags. Pending deployment and operations feedback.
